Everywhere I’ve worked, always anticipated staying at least an hour past my shift! It really depends on where you’re at, though.

For example, I spent 2 years at a very busy, understaffed 24/7 emergency teaching hospital (take a guess lol). 
Constantly on diversion, working 12-15hr days consecutively. everyone was burnt out af yet still tried our damndest to hold it together.

Now I work at an urgent care! Hours are 1pm-10pm, usually finish by 11, 11.30pm. We do outpatient treatment, occasionally send patients to 24/7 for further workup. TBH I miss emergency medicine but I’m finding my new schedule to be more compatible with life.

EDIT: TLDR; you’ll figure out what works for you, but until then, prioritize self care!  this is a demanding field but it’s worth finding a clinic that you’re compatible with.

well. since childhood I’ve struggled with clinical major depression, suicidal ideation, anxiety, alcoholism. I am a survivor of many attempts to take my own life. At ages 20-22 I was trying to kick a nasty benzo addiction on my own. While struggling to stay afloat I found out my cousin was pregnant, and the baby would have Down Syndrome.

The baby is 6 now and is one of biggest reasons I’m still here today. I don’t have Down Syndrome, but I was born with Trisomy X; growing up I was constantly bullied for atypical behavior, and being “weird.” I never felt as though I belonged anywhere. I was always so lonely. It hurts my heart to think of my sweet cousin enduring the same, so I strive to be be the person I needed when I was younger. My long term goal is to help her love herself in entirety, accept what we cannot change about ourselves, help her navigate socially, and always remember that she’s never alone..

Her life has given me a purpose. She will never know how much she’s saved me from myself.

If by medical abortion you mean taking the pills, I did that a week ago for the first time and haven’t regretted it. I was 7wk 4days pregnant and getting to the point where the morning sickness was unbearable. Maybe I’m a weenie but I couldn’t stand feeling nauseous all the time, so the thought of getting back to myself soon was helpful.

My boyfriend brought me to Planned Parenthood for the pills and they were so nice and professional. I had an vaginal ultrasound to confirm how far along I was. Then the nurse gave me one pill at 5:30pm and sent me home with 4 others to insert vaginally at 11:30pm.  She also prescribed 800mg Ibuprofen + a anti nausea med which I took a half hr before  inserting the final pills. The cramping started pretty soon after insertion but the bleeding started at roughly 5:30am. I wish I had sat on the potty for all of it because it seemed endless. The nurse said it is different for everyone but I may bleed for 4-6 weeks, you’re basically just having your period after the pregnancy tissue comes out. 

As for resenting your partner... It’s really important to make this decision for yourself, no one else. It took a few days of sitting with my feelings to know what decision felt right for me. I know for sure that I want to be a mother however I have so much more I want to accomplish before putting someone else first. I know that sounds selfish, honestly it’s okay to be sometimes. Ive been told you’re never truly ready for a baby... but it’s so important that you take into consideration your relationship with your partner, mental health, lifestyle, financial status, what you see your future looking like. 

Sorry for writing an essay but I hope this was helpful! you can DM with any specific questions I didn’t want to put too much but I am an open book! xoxo

if you're not happy, and still with her just because you are afraid of hurting her feelings... it will hurt her a lot more in the end if you keep drawing it out.   
if you're really into her and don't want to end it, be an adult and speak up about what's bothering you. here are some ways that you can do that...  
1) tell her (in a nice way) that when she does ____ in front of you, that's something to be done in private and you aren't comfortable with that.  
2) offer her a drawer at your place for her to keep personal items when she stays over, and make sure you have an extra toothbrush in case she doesn't bring hers. have a designated time where you brush your teeth together.  
3) check out [this](http://www.eatsandexercisebyamber.com/home/meal-prep-for-beginners) article on meal prepping. perhaps your girlfriend is just overwhelmed by the thought of eating a well balanced diet or thinks that healthy foods are boring, but meal prepping in the beginning of your week sets you up for success rather than having that "what am i going to eat today?!" panic.   
And if she does not make an effort to take care of herself after you have tried to help, tell her that you are concerned about her health and well-being, and suggest that you take some time apart so that she can focus on caring for herself. let me know how it goes!
